Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

active adjective

energetic, busy

also energetic, lively, busy (always doing something), physically active

classical

Cic. Verr. 2.5.27: sē praebēbat patientem atque impigrum (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Fam. 2.1.1: in scrībendō
Traupman 152

impiger, impigra, impigrum

adjective, declension

active, energetic, tireless

“Not lazy” (in- + piger), so active and untiring.

Other words

  • vegetus, vegeta, vegetum — lively, vigorous, full of life

    adjective, declension · also used · classical · Cic. Att. 10.16.6: tē vegetum nōbīs in Graeciā siste (Lewis & Short); Liv. 22.47.10: recentibus ac vegetīs

    Of someone fresh and in good health, an old person still active, troops not yet tired.

  • strēnuus, strēnua, strēnuum — brisk, vigorous, active

    adjective, declension · also used · classical · Cato Agr. praef. 3: mercātor strēnuus (Lewis & Short); Ter. Ph. 3.1.12: homō

    Of energetic people, often in war or business; also brave.

  • alacer, alacris, alacre — lively, brisk, eager

    declension · also used · classical · Ter. Eun. 304; Cic. (Lewis & Short); Traupman 268

  • nāvus (gnāvus), nāva, nāvum — energetic, hard-working

    also used · classical · Traupman 310

  • āctīvus, āctīva, āctīvum — practical (as against contemplative); active (of verbs)

    adjective, declension · avoid · post-classical · Sen. Ep. 95.10: philosophia et contemplātīva est et āctīva (Lewis & Short)

    A term of the philosophers and grammarians, the active life and the active voice; not used of a busy or energetic person.

Examples

  • tē vegetum nōbīs in Graeciā siste

    be there for us in Greece in good formCic. Att. 10.16.6 (Lewis & Short)

  • sē praebēbat patientem atque impigrum

    he showed himself patient and tirelessCic. Verr. 2.5.27 (Lewis & Short)

  • Avus octōgintā annōs nātus etiamnunc vegetus est.

    Grandpa is eighty and still very active.composed

See also efficient, lazy, eager.
